canonical_name: Killellan AI Growth Zone (Killellan Farm, Toward)
summary: Marketed hyperscale AI campus at Killellan Farm, Toward, on the Cowal peninsula south of Dunoon (not Kintyre — the similarly named Killean in Kintyre is a different place). Argyll Data Development Ltd and Argyll Energy Development Ltd (two small companies registered at the farm, directors Peter Griffiths and landowner Robert Mitchell) bid in May 2025 for UK Government AI Growth Zone designation of a 184-acre quarry-and-farmland site, and in October 2025 announced a strategic partnership with SambaNova Systems claiming a 100-600 MW first phase, 2 GW+ full build-out and £15bn investment. The only planning consent that exists is a 2020 delegated permission (20/00229/PP) for a single data-storage building of modest scale, kept alive by a March 2025 certificate of lawful commencement; no application, PAN, screening or scoping for the main campus has been located on the Argyll and Bute portal. The sovereign AI cloud 'launched' in May 2026 runs from other, undisclosed UK data centres. The gap between headline claims (up to 10 GW connectivity, £15bn) and consented reality (one small building; a developer-stated 6 MW grid application) is the largest in this dataset.
maturity_explanation: The marketed 100-600 MW / 2 GW+ campus is concept-stage: no planning application, PAN, EIA screening or scoping for it exists on the Argyll and Bute portal as of 30 Jul 2026. The only consent is 20/00229/PP (approved 15 May 2020) for one Class 4 data-storage building, with lawful commencement certified via 25/00445/CLAWU (28 Mar 2025). That small consented element alone might merit M3, but it is not the announced project; the campus itself is M0 with M1 features (land control, AI Growth Zone bid, initial £15m raise).
anticipated_construction_start: Developer states first (2020-consented) building operational by 2026 subject to funding; no dates for main campus
anticipated_operational_date: Developer claim: 500 MW operational by 2030 (AI Growth Zone bid); unverified

phases.description: Single building permitted under 20/00229/PP; developer-stated first connection of 6 MW; developer anticipated operational 2026 subject to funding
Long-term vision of up to 10 GW connectivity supporting 2-3 GW active capacity with triple redundancy
